title: Adani Power Profit Jumps 42% to Record ₹4,806 Crore as India's Power Appetite Hits New Peaks
excerpt: India's largest private thermal power producer reported its strongest-ever quarter, driven by a scorching summer that pushed national electricity consumption up nearly 9%.
body:
• Adani Power reported a 42% year-on-year jump in consolidated net profit to ₹4,806 crore for Q1 FY27, its highest-ever quarterly performance on both operating and financial metrics.
  • Revenue from operations surged 34% to ₹18,902 crore, with power sales volume rising 17% to a record 28.8 billion units.
  • India's electricity consumption grew 8.8% year-on-year during the quarter to 485 billion units, driven by a hotter-than-usual summer.
  • The board approved raising up to ₹15,000 crore through equity issuance via a qualified institutional placement or other routes.

Adani Power, India's largest private-sector thermal power generator, delivered its strongest quarter on record in the three months ended June 30, as a brutally hot summer drove national electricity demand to new highs and the company's expanded capacity ran at its highest utilisation rates in years.

Consolidated net profit attributable to equity holders rose 42% year-on-year to ₹4,806 crore, up from ₹3,385 crore in Q1 FY26, according to the company's exchange filing. Revenue from operations climbed 34% to ₹18,902 crore. EBITDA surged 36% to ₹8,369 crore, while continuing EBITDA — which strips out one-time items — came in at ₹6,983 crore, up 22% from the year-ago period.

Scorching Demand, Record Generation

The quarter's performance was built on a simple foundation: India needed more electricity, and Adani Power was positioned to supply it. The company's power sales volume rose 17% year-on-year to 28.8 billion units, while power generation touched a record 31 billion units during the quarter.

Nationally, electricity consumption jumped 8.8% during the April-June period to 485 billion units, according to the company, driven by an unusually severe summer across large parts of India. Air conditioning load, industrial activity, and the broader electrification of the Indian economy all contributed to the demand surge.

"The company recorded its highest-ever quarterly operating and financial performance, supported by rising electricity demand, higher power generation and improved capacity utilisation."

— Adani Power, exchange filing

Installed generation capacity grew to 18,330 MW from 17,550 MW a year ago. More tellingly, the plant load factor — the key measure of how hard a power company runs its assets — improved dramatically to 77.9%, up from 67% in Q1 FY26. That 11-percentage-point jump reflects both the demand pull and better operational execution.

Capital Raise to Fund Expansion

Alongside the results, Adani Power's board approved raising up to ₹15,000 crore through the issuance of equity shares via a qualified institutional placement or other permissible routes. The capital raise signals the company's intent to continue expanding generation capacity to meet India's growing power needs.

India's power sector has been on a sustained expansion trajectory. The country added roughly 26 GW of generation capacity in FY26, and the government's target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030 is driving investment across both thermal and renewable assets. For thermal producers like Adani Power, the near-term economics remain favourable: coal-fired generation continues to provide the baseload that intermittent renewables cannot yet fully replace.

Market Reaction and Outlook

Despite the record results, Adani Power shares slipped about 1.4% on the day of the announcement, closing at ₹217.31. The muted market response likely reflects the stock's strong run in recent months and broader caution around the Adani Group following last year's regulatory scrutiny.

For India's energy sector, the quarter underscores a structural reality: the country's power demand growth shows no sign of slowing. With GDP growth running above 6%, urbanisation accelerating, and data centres emerging as a major new source of electricity consumption, the investment case for Indian power infrastructure remains one of the clearest in Asia's emerging markets.
